Commentary.Commentary: This brings us to the end of Match number 5 then. We didn't get any cricket from this clash, but the conditions have gotten a bit brighter in Kuala Lumpur and the covers too, are coming off gradually. So we will get to see some cricket as Match number 6 is about to take place between India Women Under-19 and Bangladesh Women Under-19. The first ball will be bowled at 6.30 am GMT at the same venue. Both teams have arrived at the ground and we hope that the weather won't play any spoilsport in that clash. But from here, that is it! Do switch the tabs to get all the pre-match excitement of the next match. Cheers!

Well then, this match has been called off without the toss and both teams will get one point each. This also marks the end of the journey for Scotland Women Under-19 in this ICC Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup as it is not possible for them to reach the top two. They still have a couple of games remaining though, and would want to finish their campaign on a positive note, and of course, with a lot of learning. For Sri Lanka though, they too, would've wanted to get two crucial points, but they still remain in the race for the semifinals. They take the third position with three points in three games in Group A.

UPDATE - 4.30 am GMT - There comes the dreaded news, folks! MATCH NUMBER 5 OF THE SUPER SIX STAGE HAS BEEN ABANDONED DUE TO RAIN. The match officials communicated to both captains and they shook their hands to call off this match. It's a shame that we couldn't get any cricket between Sri Lanka Women Under-19 and Scotland Women Under-19 in Group A. This means that both teams will share one point each.

UPDATE - 4.16 am GMT - The rain seems to have slowed down now fair bit, and the match officials are out there for an unofficial inspection. Both the captains are also out there, but they're in their training gear and are having some chatter. Fair to say, that the ground conditions are pretty damp out there and the covers remain firm in the middle. Also, as per the on-air commentators, 4.57 am GMT is the cut-off time for this game to start, which is about half an hour from now. The conditions still remain dark overhead. We still stay hopeful to get some action from this game. Stay tuned.

UPDATE - 3.55 am GMT - We have lost more than an hour and a half now, which means, potentially an entire inning. But unfortunately, it is still heavily raining out there and with every passing minute, the chances of any cricket today are getting bleaker now. If we go by the weather forecast, the inevitable might be upon us. However, we still stay hopeful about getting some cricket at least. Stay tuned for further updates.

UPDATE - 3.16 am GMT - The rain continues to pelt down heavily in Kuala Lumpur and the Bayuemas Oval remains to be covered heavily under the sheets. And just as per the on-air commentators, we have already started to lose overs. One of the umpires is out but with the umbrella wide open over the head. We can already see a few puddles forming near the boundary ropes, which is not a good sign as it takes a good chunk of time to dry up. Unfortunately, for now, we remain optimistic that conditions will get better soon. Stay tuned for further updates.

UPDATE - 2.32 am GMT - Oh, dear! It seems like we are here for a long, long delay. It is gotten more heavy now and the forecast for the rest of the day does not look promising either. This means, that the second match of the day, between India Women Under-19 and Bangladesh Women Under-19 is also under the scare of a delay. All we can do is hope that the rain subsides soon and the ground is ready for cricket. But that seems unlikely seeing the heavy showers in Kuala Lumpur. We will get back to you with more updates. Stay tuned and keep your fingers crossed.

UPDATE - 2.18 am GMT - We know you all must've been eagerly waiting for the toss and team updates, but, unfortunately, we are here to give you the dreaded update. IT IS RAINING IN KUALA LUMPUR. The entire ground is under the sheets right now as it is pelting down really heavily. There's no movement whatsoever on the ground and it is threateningly dark overhead as well. We just hope the conditions get better soon. Stay tuned for all the updates.ra

Sri Lanka enters this clash as a strong favorite, thanks to their balanced team and standout performances so far. However, Scotland has shown resilience and flashes of brilliance that could pose a challenge. The key battle will be between Sri Lanka’s formidable bowlers, led by Chamodi Praboda, and Scotland’s fragile batting order. Can Scotland spring a surprise and push the Asian giants to their limits? Or will Sri Lanka continue their dominant run in the tournament? This promises to be an exciting match to watch! Stay tuned for Toss and other match updates.

Scotland’s campaign has been a mix of highs and lows. Finishing third in Group D, they have faced two heavy defeats but showed promise with a strong win over Nepal. Wicket-keeper batter Pippa Sproul has been their standout performer, scoring 35 and 43 in the group stage, providing stability at the crease. However, the rest of the batting lineup has struggled for consistency, and they will need to step up against a potent Sri Lankan bowling attack. Maisie Maceira has been the shining star in the bowling department, claiming a five-wicket haul earlier in the tournament. For Scotland to challenge Sri Lanka, they will need both batters and bowlers to deliver collectively.

Sri Lanka have been a dominant force in the tournament so far, finishing second in Group A, one of the toughest pools. Their journey includes two commanding victories against West Indies and Malaysia, while their only loss came against the formidable India team. The Sri Lankan side has excelled in all areas of the game. The batting lineup has been bolstered by consistent contributions from Sanjana Kavindi at the top and Dahami Sanethma in the middle order. Skipper Manudi Nayanakka has also chipped in with crucial runs, adding depth to their batting strength.

Both teams have navigated different paths to reach this stage, and this encounter is set to be a crucial contest for both sides.

The Super Six stage of the ICC Women’s Under-19 is in full tilt and Match number 5 promises more excitement as Sri Lanka Women take on the Scotland Women. The Bayuemas Oval of Kuala Lumpur will serve as the host for this crucial clash. Finishing second in one of the toughest pools of teams, Sri Lanka were a dominant force in Group A. Their journey so far has been marked by two comprehensive wins against West Indies and Malaysia, and a humbling defeat to India. Sri Lankans have shown remarkable performances in all facets of the game. Ably supported by batters like Sanjana Kavindi up top and Dahami Sanethma in the middle order, the team has a good composition with skipper Manudi Nayanakka too among the runs. Replicating their batting dominance, Chamodi Praboda has spearheaded the bowling department in fine fashion. Snagging a three-fer against West Indies and then repeating the same against Malaysia, she has been the linchpin in the bowling department and also finds herself in the tournament’s leading wicket-takers. Finishing third in the group D, Scotland Women have had their fair share of troubles on the way to the next stage. With their two heavy defeats, they can draw out some positives from their solitary win against a strong Nepal side. Wicket-keeper batter Pippa Sproul has been in the thick of runs and has shown flashes of brilliance with scores of 35 and 43 so far, but the test remains on the rest of the batters to step up responsibly. Maisie Maceira has been their standout bowler with a five-fer already in the tournament. However, the onus lies on the batters about how do they come to terms with a dangerous Sri Lankan bowling unit. Will the Scottish girls throw a stern challenge to the Asian giant Sri Lanka? It’s promising to be a clash to watch out for!
